disk noun

for storing data, or a CD

also disc, hard disk, hard drive, floppy disk, CD, compact disc, DVD, disk drive

Traupman 260, 305
M-O s.v. CD

discus, discī m.

noun, second declension

a disk (of a computer); a disc

Traupman’s word for a computer disk; Morgan–Owens gives discus mūsicus for a music CD. Classically discus is a quoit, thrown in the games (Hor. C. 1.8.11), then a dish shaped like one (Apul.) and the disc of a sundial (Vitr. 9.9.1); its modern sense keeps the shape.

Other words

  • dūra statiō — a hard drive

    also used · modern · Traupman 261, 326

    Traupman’s phrase, a calque of the English. Where a disk is meant, discus serves as well.

  • 1compāctus: long a (Traupman 260 leaves it unmarked). From compingō (from com- and pangō), which has its participle from the root of pangō: Lachmann’s law, as pāctus. Ruling: Lachmann’s law: āctus, lēctus, frāctus.

    compāctus discus1 — a CD, compact disc

    also used · modern · Traupman 260, 294

  • disculus, disculī m. — a diskette, a floppy disk

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 260, 305, 316

    A diminutive of discus; Lewis & Short has no such word.

  • discus digitālis — a DVD

    also used · modern · Andresian p. 15; Traupman 308: digitālis disculus

See also computer, hardware, save.
